value.a: THE SURVIVAL RULE DIVERGES FROM ORIENT'S DELIBERATELY, AND MIRRORING WOULD HAVE SHIPPED A CONSTANT. orient compares floor to ceiling by SET EQUALITY, which is right there because refs is a complete lookup result. constraints is not that shape: it is multi-source by construction — 148 charter, 110 ticket, 63 law, 33 ruling, 14 memory over 394 live items — and the floor owns exactly one kind. I built equality first, mirroring orient, and MEASURED 39 of 39 candidate packets reading 'claude' with no reachable path to anything else. The rule became two-sided: the floor's items survive unchanged AND no other charter-kind constraint appears beside them. Survival alone catches a DROPPED constraint and not a FORGED one, which is why both clauses are load-bearing.

'NOT A COMPONENT' WAS FOUR FINDINGS WEARING ONE SENTENCE, and they are now told apart in unknowns: an ambiguous NAME (two components share it, so the roster cannot answer); a roster/lookup disagreement (the roster says yes and resolution says no, which is a defect in the corpus rather than in the ref); a string naming neither a component nor a path that exists on disk (a stale pointer); and a real path that sits under NO component, so no charter bounds it (commons files, skills, top-level scripts). The first two are red, the last two are ordinary. Collapsing them hands a reader a sentence instead of a diagnosis.

THE 24 EMPTY-FLOOR PACKETS ARE HONEST AND THE BUILD SAYS SO. Their refs name paths retired by the 2026-08-13 rung move (115 of them) or commons and skill files under no component (47). That is the world having moved, not the floor failing, and it is recorded here so a later reader does not re-diagnose it.

THE DUPLICATE THAT WAS INVISIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION. Once path refs resolved, a component named BOTH by name and by path in the same orient packet produced every one of its constraints twice. It could not have been seen before, because a discarded ref cannot collide — and it could not be seen by reading the output either, since the duplicate texts are identical and read as a longer list of correct answers. A count tooth caught it; inspection would not have.

A PROOF CAN BE GREEN ABOUT A WORLD THAT NO LONGER EXISTS. constrain's fixture still built the flat cairn/<name>/ house that the rung move retired on 2026-08-13, and nothing redded because the component walk still finds a non-rung directory at top level. With every fixture component one level down, the deepest-owner rule had nothing to be wrong about — the fixture was testing an easier world than the real one.

THE SOURCE SPELLING WAS MINE TO FIX AND THE JUDGE WAS NOT. The floor first packed <path>#<field> into a constraint's source, and the installed judge refused all six, because it resolves a source through the one ref-resolution semantics the berth gate uses. The field moved to its own key rather than teaching that judge about fragments — a second spelling of 'where does this point' in a component this module is forbidden to shape (Law 6).

THIS TICKET IS STUCK AT TICKETME AND THE CODE IS DONE, PROVEN AND SEALED — RECORDED RATHER THAN ROUTED AROUND. The BUILDME crossing was refused by its own entry gate on 2026-08-14, verbatim: 'no berthed chart chain claims ticket constrain-floor-authors-and-provenance-is-measured — the build has no charted course'. THE GATE IS RIGHT. I built first and cast the ticket afterwards, so the preamble the chain exists to compile was never compiled and the build did not run inside it. The available fix is to run /chart now, and it is PLASTER: berths written after the build satisfy the check without establishing the thing it checks for, which is the hollow pass Law 8 exists to refuse. So the boat stays at TICKETME until the order is right, and the disposition is forward rather than retroactive — SURVEY IS CHARTED BEFORE IT IS BUILT. That also settles what the chain runs on: charting survey's own build fires stage 2, which is constrain, and berths the first post-door constrain packets the WATCHME above is waiting for.

ORIENT REACHED PROVED ONLY BECAUSE ITS TICKET FILE WAS AUTHORED PAST THIS GATE, and that is the same defect one rung up rather than a precedent. MEASURED across the 41 tickets ever cast through /sorted: 40 carry an intent_berth and orient's is the only one that carries none, and git shows its file was first committed with its cursor already at [BUILDME] — a position no crossing ever moved it to, because the /sorted door refuses a cast cursor past TICKETME and the ticket FILE has no door at all. So the entry gate never fired on it. This is the casting-has-no-chokepoint IOU already named in cairn/tools/base/watchme_spec.py, with its n=2 now measured rather than predicted; the seven other tickets born past TICKETME all carry an intent_berth, so the corpus is not generally leaking — these two builds are.

COMPONENT_OF BELONGS IN base AND NOT IN constrain, and the reason is not tidiness. It is the other half of a question the corpus already asks in two places and answers in one; AmbiguousComponent's error text has been promising the behaviour to readers who had no way to get it. Written with Path.expanduser so cairn/tools/base keeps importing pathlib and nothing else — a property constrain's own import site measures and leans on, which a convenience import would have quietly cost.
